terms.gloss: draw out, take out (money from where it is kept)
terms.grammar: pecūniam ex arcā, ex aerāriō; ē māchinā nummāriā
evidence: Cic. Imp. Pomp. 37: pecūniam, ex aerāriō dēprōmptam ad bellum administrandum
Cic. Off. 2.52: altera ex arcā, altera ex virtūte dēprōmitur
terms.comment: The verb for fetching a thing out of a store, and so for money taken from a strongbox or the treasury. Of a bank or a cash machine (see “cash machine”) its use is ours.

phrases.latin: altera ex arcā, altera ex virtūte dēprōmitur
phrases.english: the one is drawn from the strongbox, the other from character

phrases.latin: Ē māchinā nummāriā quīnquāgintā nummōs dēprōmpsī.
phrases.english: I took fifty euros out of the cash machine.

phrases.latin: Pecūnia in argentāriā est; crās dēprōmam.
phrases.english: The money’s in the bank; I’ll take it out tomorrow.
